## The question

[Area of shaded curve integral negative thus incorrect](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/5008975/area-of-shaded-curve-integral-negative-thus-incorrect), asked by [Sara Jönsson](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/1472781/sara-j%c3%b6nsson) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2024-12-08; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Find the area of the shaded figure, integral.
>
> [![enter image description here][q-1]][q-1]
>
> **Integral:**
>
> $$\int_{a}^{b} (x^2-4) \, dx$$
>
> **Limitations:**
>
> $y=x^2-4$
>
> $x^2-4=0$
>
> $x^2=4$
>
> $x = \pm \sqrt{4} = 2$
>
> The limitation I am able to find from the figure,$\left[-2, 2\right]$.
>
> **Integrating:**
>
> $\int_{-2}^{2} (x^2-4) \, dx = \left[\frac{x^3}{3} - 4x\right]_{-2}^{2}$
>
> **Applying:**
>
> $F(2)-F(-2) = -\frac{16}{3} - \frac{16}{3}$
>
> $=-\frac{32}{3}$
>
> My answer was wrong, according to the back of the book the correct solution is: **$\frac{32}{3}$**, mine is negative.
>
>
>   [q-1]: LhXtrNdr.jpg
:::

The integral is correct, but it doesn't compute the area of the shaded region. If $f(x) \geq 0$, then $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ computes the area of region satisfying $a\leq x \leq b$ and $0 \leq y \leq f(x)$. 

In general, if $f(x) \leq g(x)$ on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b (g(x)-f(x))\,dx$ measures the area of the region satisfying $0 \leq x \leq b$ and $f(x) \leq y \leq g(x)$. If you set $g(x) = 0$ you will get the right area.
